content:
kai: Quick decision check — for Private tenants are we favouring a per-tenant egress gateway (one ENI/NAT per tenant) or a shared regional gateway with tenant-to-EIP mapping? Main blockers: preserving original client IP for SAML/webhooks and audit logs, plus AZ failover semantics.

sree: My bias is per-tenant for security/audit reasons, but cost and ENI limits are the obvious tradeoff. How many tenants do we expect to hit ENI/EIP limits? :thinking_face:

maya: Per-tenant keeps source IP at the network layer, which is nice for allowlists. Shared + `X-Forwarded-For` only helps apps that we control; external partners won't see the real source. Also AWS EIP scarcity for large fleets is real.

devon: Could we do shared gateway but allocate a small sticky pool of EIPs per-tenant and do deterministic SNAT mapping? That avoids per-tenant ENIs but gives each tenant stable egress IPs. Concern: conntrack table scaling and port exhaustion.

sree: Exactly — sticky SNAT in conntrack needs careful testing. Cold bursts could force port reuse; cross-AZ failover would reassign EIP and break existing flows.

kai: Sketch of a hybrid: lightweight per-tenant "ambassador" (sidecar-like) that preserves original source via an `X-Original-Client-IP` header for apps that can read it, while performing SNAT to allocated EIP for external allowlists. Infrastructure logs can include the header via our ingress parsing. That keeps audits usable without 1:1 ENI.

maya: Example SNAT rule we spun up in the spike (for reference):
```
# allocate a single EIP per tenant and SNAT outbound
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.100.0.0/24 -j SNAT --to-source 3.52.120.22
# preserve X-Forwarded-For in the ambassador proxy
```
This makes the proxy explicit about "who" initiated the connection.

devon: Routing alternative note: PrivateLink/interface endpoints are inbound for us — they don't change outbound egress. Cannot rely on them for source IP preservation.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pipeline triggered: `egress-affinity-proxy` -> staging (run-42). Check logs: https://ci.internal/runs/42 :rocket:

sree: Decision criteria i'm tracking: 1) preserve original IP for customer security/audit, 2) stable egress IP for allowlists, 3) cost & ENI/EIP limits, 4) failover semantics (AZ flips), 5) operational complexity and SRE burden.

kai: Proposed actions: 1) short perf/cost spike to quantify ENI/EIP at scale (run with 5k simulated tenants), 2) conntrack/port-utilization spike for sticky SNAT, 3) implement ambassador prototype that injects `X-Original-Client-IP` and measure app compatibility. I'll own 1+3.

devon: I'll own the conntrack test and share a frag report by EOD Friday.

maya: If the spike shows ENI/EIP cost is prohibitive, we default to shared gateway + ambassador + clear docs for partners about header reliance. Consider an enterprise-only per-tenant paid add-on for full network-level IP preservation.

kai: Sounds good. @sree / @devon please comment if you want this escalated to arch RFC or we keep it as an ops-design follow-up.

sree: Keep as ops follow-up unless the spike surfaces a hard networking constraint. For transparency I'll add the decision criteria to the repo's architecture board. :+1:

kai: Thanks — closing thread for now. Follow-ups in the spike PR and staging canary logs.
